title: Algebra-sheaf image factorization agrees with the underlying module image
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $\psi:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ a morphism of commutative $\mathcal O$-algebra sheaves [def-weil-pbc-ringed-space-algebra-module]. For an open $U$, let $\mathcal D(U)$ consist of those $a\in\mathcal A(U)$ such that every $x\in U$ has an open neighbourhood $V\subseteq U$ and $b\in\mathcal B(V)$ with $a|_V=\psi_V(b)$. With restrictions and operations inherited from $\mathcal A$, $\mathcal D$ is a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O$-algebras. There are canonical algebra maps $p:\mathcal B\to\mathcal D$ and $i:\mathcal D\to\mathcal A$ with $ip=\psi$, where $i$ is sectionwise injective and $p$ is locally surjective (every section of $\mathcal D$ lifts through $p$ on an open covering). The underlying module of $\mathcal D$, with this inclusion into $\mathcal A$, is canonically the categorical image of the underlying $\mathcal O$-linear map [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Moreover, for every factorization $\psi=jf$ through an algebra sheaf $\mathcal H$ with $j:\mathcal H\to\mathcal A$ sectionwise injective, there is a unique algebra map $k:\mathcal D\to\mathcal H$ with $jk=i$ and $kp=f$.

source.place: Tag 0087, lemma-sheafify-presheaf-structures, together with Modules Tag 01AG, lemma-abelian and the image/coimage construction preceding it: algebraic-structure image compared with module image

proof.text: Construct the local image as the sheafification of the set-valued range subfunctor of A using Mathlib Subfunctor.sheafify. Its sections form subrings: intersect covering sieves of lifts for addition and multiplication; use negatives of lifts and the images of zero and one for the remaining operations. Restriction is inherited from A. This is exactly the local-image construction of Stacks Sheaves 0087.

source.place: Tag 0087, lemma-sheafify-presheaf-structures: local algebraic operations, written out for the local image

proof.text: Use Mathlib Subfunctor.sheafify_isSheaf and Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_comp for the commutative-ring forgetful functor to obtain a ring sheaf D. Its structure map is O to B followed by range restriction. Inclusion i and range restriction p give p followed by i equal to psi; inclusion is sectionwise injective.

source.place: Tag 0087, lemma-sheafify-presheaf-structures: sheaf gluing in the underlying sheaf of sets

proof.text: On underlying sheaves of sets, p and i are the Mathlib Sheaf.toImage and Sheaf.imageι maps. Mathlib proves local surjectivity of toImage. Translate a covering sieve into a neighborhood of each point; choose these neighborhoods indexed by the points of U to obtain the stated cover. Membership in the sheafified range is precisely the neighborhood local-lift condition. The point-indexed cover is empty when U is empty.

source.place: Tag 0087, lemma-sheafify-presheaf-structures: canonical algebra maps in the local-image construction

proof.text: Apply the underlying-module functor and then SheafOfModules.toSheaf to the underlying abelian sheaves. The inclusion has injective section maps, so its underlying sheaf map is monic by Sheaf.mono_of_injective. The projection is locally surjective because local surjectivity is unchanged by forgetting algebraic structure (Presheaf.isLocallySurjective_iff_whisker_forget), so its underlying abelian sheaf map is epic by Sheaf.epi_of_isLocallySurjective. The faithful underlying-sheaf functor reflects these mono and epi properties.

source.place: Tag 01AG, lemma-abelian, and Section 01AF, section-kernels: module epimorphisms are local surjections

proof.text: The module category is abelian by Mathlib SheafOfModules.instAbelian, since the site of opens and section modules lie in the same universe. Its epimorphisms are strong (strongEpi_of_epi). Apply image.isoStrongEpiMono to the module factorization to obtain the desired canonical image isomorphism. Its inclusion equation is image.isoStrongEpiMono_hom_comp_ι; cancel the monic image inclusion to prove the equation for p.

source.place: Tag 0106, definition-kernel (image is kernel of cokernel); abelian-category kernel property as stated in def-sp-abelian

proof.text: For any algebra factorization through a sectionwise injective j, pass to sheaves of sets. The monic factorization is a MonoFactorisation, so Mathlib imageFactorization.isImage.lift supplies a map k from the set image sheaf to H, with j composed with k equal to inclusion. Since j is injective on sections and preserves ring operations, this equation implies preservation of zero, one, sums and products by k. Its inherited naturality makes k a ring-sheaf morphism.

source.place: Tag 0087, lemma-sheafify-presheaf-structures: local lifts and unique gluing for the factorization

proof.text: Cancel j to show the map from the preceding step respects O, giving an algebra-sheaf morphism. Cancellation proves compatibility with p from the original factorization equality, and proves uniqueness from k followed by j equal to i.

lean.statement: theorem commAlgebraSheaf_image_factorization {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] (O : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) CommRingCat.{u}) {B A : Under O} (ψ : B ⟶ A) : ∃ (D : Under O) (p : B ⟶ D) (i : D ⟶ A), p ≫ i = ψ ∧ (∀ U : Opens X, Function.Injective (i.right.hom.app (op U))) ∧ (∀ (U : Opens X) (a : A.right.obj.obj (op U)), (∃ d : D.right.obj.obj (op U), i.right.hom.app (op U) d = a) ↔ ∀ x : U, ∃ (V : Opens X) (hV : V ≤ U), (x : X) ∈ V ∧ ∃ b : B.right.obj.obj (op V), A.right.obj.map (homOfLE hV).op a = ψ.right.hom.app (op V) b) ∧ (∀ (U : Opens X) (d : D.right.obj.obj (op U)), ∃ (I : Type u) (V : I → Opens X) (hV : ∀ t, V t ≤ U) (b : ∀ t, B.right.obj.obj (op (V t))), (⨆ t, V t) = U ∧ ∀ t, p.right.hom.app (op (V t)) (b t) = D.right.obj.map (homOfLE (hV t)).op d) ∧ (∃ e : (commAlgebraSheafModuleFunctor O).obj D ≅ image ((commAlgebraSheafModuleFunctor O).map ψ), e.hom ≫ image.ι ((commAlgebraSheafModuleFunctor O).map ψ) = (commAlgebraSheafModuleFunctor O).map i ∧ (commAlgebraSheafModuleFunctor O).map p ≫ e.hom = factorThruImage ((commAlgebraSheafModuleFunctor O).map ψ)) ∧ (∀ (H : Under O) (f : B ⟶ H) (j : H ⟶ A), (∀ U : Opens X, Function.Injective (j.right.hom.app (op U))) → f ≫ j = ψ → ∃! k : D ⟶ H, k ≫ j = i ∧ p ≫ k = f)
